title: Data keeps its units, kind and precision
statement: Label invented data as invented, keep its units and scale, tell counts, rates, percentages and indices apart, and never let a qualitative model become a number it can't support.
detail: A Grade 5 reading course's generation contract makes this a cross-unit rule for four of its units: a qualitative model cannot silently become a quantitative claim, and invented classroom indices cannot be presented as measurements. The course's passages do use invented data, such as an invented climate-normal table set beside two reports and a relief map, so the rule governs real material. It goes beyond labelling an invented source: the units, the scale and the kind of number stay as stated, and no figure claims more precision than its source supports.
